analysis.purpose: runCliResult is a test helper that runs the CLI binary and returns a structured result object containing exit status, stdout, and stderr. Unlike runCli, it catches non-zero exits and surfaces them as a normal status value, making it useful for testing error paths without throwing.
responsibilities: Execute the CLI binary synchronously in the test repository
Normalize successful and failed executions into a single {status, stdout, stderr} shape
Trim captured stdout and stderr before returning them

businessRules.rationale: The happy path explicitly returns status: 0 when execFileSync completes without throwing

businessRules.rule: Failed executions report status from the caught error or default to 1
businessRules.rationale: The catch branch uses err.status ?? 1 to preserve non-zero exit codes while ensuring a defined status

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: CLI arguments to pass after the script path

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Structured CLI execution result with normalized status and trimmed streams

sideEffects: Spawns a synchronous child process via execFileSync
errorBehavior: Catches execFileSync exceptions and converts them into a result object using the error's status, stdout, and stderr fields
invariants: Returned stdout and stderr are always trimmed
Returned status is always a number (0 on success, err.status or 1 on failure)
preconditions: The CLI script at path `CLI` must be executable by `process.execPath`
The caught error object, if any, may optionally expose status, stdout, and stderr properties
postconditions: A structured result is returned for both successful and failing CLI executions
risks: Type cast `e as {status?: number; ...}` could hide runtime shapes that do not match the ExecFileSync error contract
Unresolved execFileSync call means exact throw/catch behavior is not modeled in the graph
whatToDistrust: execFileSync and trim are unresolved built-in calls
The exact type/runtime shape of the caught error is cast, not validated
